Although the preprocessor will happily do so, you should generally not #include .cpp files. These should be added to your project and compiled.

There are number of reasons for this:

1. Doing so can cause naming collisions between source files.
2. In a large project it can be hard to avoid one definition rules (ODR) issues.
3. Any change to such a .cpp file will cause both the .cpp file and any other .cpp file that includes it to recompile, which can take a long time. Headers tend to change less often than source files.
4. It is non-conventional to do so.
